source_caption:
The breathtaking, incredibly romantic climax of the film—where Mr. Darcy emerges from the morning mist to confess that Elizabeth Bennet has bewitched him “body and soul”—was significantly less majestic to actually film. In real life, Matthew Macfadyen has notoriously terrible eyesight and is practically blind without his glasses. Because he wasn’t wearing contacts during the shoot, and the thick early-morning fog drastically reduced visibility, Macfadyen couldn’t actually see Keira Knightley or the cameras waiting for him across the field. To keep him from wandering off in the wrong direction, director Joe Wright had to stand directly behind the camera waving a bright red flag just so Macfadyen had a blurry target to aim for as he confidently strode through the dew.

Pride & Prejudice (2005), directed by Joe Wright, starring Keira Knightley, Matthew Macfadyen, Donald Sutherland, Rosamund Pike, Brenda Blethyn. Based on Jane Austen’s beloved novel, the fiercely independent Elizabeth Bennet navigates the intense societal pressures of 19th-century England and her own complicated, evolving feelings for the wealthy, notoriously proud Mr. Darcy.

source_details.synopsis: Pride & Prejudice is a 2005 period romance film directed by Joe Wright, in his feature directorial debut, based on Jane Austen's 1813 novel of the same name. The film features five sisters from an English family of landed gentry as they deal with issues of marriage, morality, and misconceptions. Keira Knightley stars as Elizabeth Bennet, while Matthew Macfadyen plays Mr Darcy, who falls in love with her. Screenwriter Deborah Moggach initially attempted to make her script as faithful to the novel as possible, writing from Elizabeth's perspective while preserving much of the original dialogue.
